strings.title: The Final Chapter
strings.hint: The novel has not been published, so how did the killer know the details of the crime in it? Find out who held the only manuscript.
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: literary editor Hala Radwan.

In her unpublished novel, the victim had written a murder that precisely described a real event: Hala's involvement in the death of her former husband years earlier, a case closed as an accident. The novelist had understood the truth from a passing confession and turned it into fiction. Hala, the only editor holding the manuscript, realized publication would reopen the old case. She killed the novelist using the method described in the final chapter, believing this would cast suspicion on any reader of the manuscript. But she was its only reader.

Her sole outside fingerprint on the secret manuscript, the murder matching a chapter nobody else had read, and the reopened file on her husband's death, matching the novel's plot, proved her guilt.
strings.summary.text: Prominent novelist Samira Najm was found murdered in her study with strange precision: strangled with a silk scarf, the scene arranged to match the final chapter of her new novel word for word. The novel had not yet been published, and only one copy existed. The killer carried out a crime written before it happened. Who had read the ending?

strings.scene.intro: A quiet study, with no forced entry. The crime matches the manuscript's final chapter down to the smallest details: the type of scarf, the body's position, even a book open at a particular page. The only manuscript was with the editor.

strings.evidence[0].title: The Secret Manuscript
strings.evidence[0].desc: The only copy. Its final chapter literally describes the crime that occurred. The only outside fingerprint on it belongs to the editor.
strings.evidence[1].title: The Silk Scarf
strings.evidence[1].desc: Exactly matches the novel's description of the murder weapon. It did not belong to the victim.
strings.evidence[2].title: The Old Death File
strings.evidence[2].desc: The editor's former husband died 6 years ago. The case was closed as an accident, but its details match the novel's plot.
strings.evidence[3].title: Publishing Contract
strings.evidence[3].desc: The novel was due to go to print within days, after which thousands would read it.
strings.evidence[4].title: Manuscript Handover Log
strings.evidence[4].desc: The manuscript was handed only to editor Hala at 18:00. No other copies were authorized.
strings.suspects[0].name: Magdi, the Publisher
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was at another author's book signing, in front of the attendees."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Samira was my publishing house's star and my best-selling author. Her death is a terrible loss. I hadn't read the novel yet. Our procedure is for the editor to review it first. The book signing proves where I was all evening.
strings.suspects[1].name: Roshdi, the Former Husband
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I was away on a business trip. My flight ticket proves it."
strings.suspects[1].statement: We separated peacefully years ago and stayed in respectful contact. There was no hostility between us worth killing over. I was abroad that night, and my passport has the arrival and departure stamps.
strings.suspects[2].name: Hala Radwan
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I took the manuscript home to review and went to bed early."
strings.suspects[2].statement: I worked with Samira for ten years and polished her finest novels. Yes, I was the only person holding the manuscript. That's my job. Linking her novel to my personal life is painful fiction. My husband died in a documented accident. Literature draws on reality. That doesn't make me a murderer.
strings.witnesses[0].name: The Victim's Assistant
strings.witnesses[0].statement: Samira excitedly told me her latest novel would "shake someone to the core" and was based on a real secret she discovered by chance. She didn't say whose.
strings.witnesses[1].name: The Novelist's Neighbor
strings.witnesses[1].statement: I saw an elegant woman carrying a briefcase enter Samira's house near ten in the evening. I recognized her: her editor, who had visited before.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Investigator of the Old Case
strings.witnesses[2].statement: The editor's husband's death six years ago was classified as a domestic accident, but some details remained unclear. Reopening it could change a great deal.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Body discovery report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The novelist's assistant reported the death. The scene was arranged with unusual care.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Autopsy report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Strangulation with soft silk fabric. Death occurred at 22:00–22:30. Little resistance: the victim was taken by surprise.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Manuscript Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: The only outside fingerprint on the final chapter belongs to editor Hala. No other reader's fingerprints were found.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Scene-to-Text Comparison
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: The crime scene details almost completely match the final chapter. Whoever staged it had read the text.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Hala Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: She denied visiting the house until confronted with the neighbor's testimony. Mention of her husband's death unsettled her.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Publisher interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: The book signing establishes his whereabouts. He had not seen the manuscript.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Former Husband Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: Passport stamps document his travel abroad.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Reexamining the Late Husband's File
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The details of Hala's husband's death match the plot of Samira's novel. The novel exposed what an old accident had concealed.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confession Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the fingerprint, the matching scene, and the old file, Hala broke down: "She wrote my crime. Publishing it would have been my death… so I got there first."
strings.reports[0].title: The Written Crime Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: A crime matching an unpublished chapter narrows the culprit to the reader of its sole copy: the editor.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The novel would have exposed the editor's old crime. Imminent publication created an existential motive for murder.
strings.notes[0].text: A crime matching an unpublished chapter. Who read it?
strings.notes[1].text: The novel is based on a real secret… whose secret?
